issue.title: what is DroneCores's uuid with multiple vehicles?

comments.body:
Thanks for the question. In my opinion, the issue here is that each drone simulated by SITL has the same UUID. UUID stands "Universally unique identifier", which means they should be unique 😄 .

One workaround for you would be to add something to the UUID in each of your instances, so that they differ from each other.

And note that you also need to set different system IDs for each of the drones.

Um.. in my case I don't use SITL.
My five drones in real case.  My five different drones have same UUID.....
Maybe it is idiot question do you have many drones?

> Um.. in my case I don't use SITL.

Oh, sorry. I was just assuming that. Ok, so what PX4 version are you using on them?
And could the issue be that DroneCore is still using the field `uid` instead of `uid2` in http://mavlink.org/messages/common#AUTOPILOT_VERSION? You can check if the `uid2` field is actually different.
We are planning to move to `uid2` in the future.

>  Maybe it is idiot question do you have many drones?

Good question 😄 . So I have a couple of drones but I have not used DroneCore with multiple drones at the same time. We've implemented it in a way to potentially support more than one but there might be some work left to get it to work properly.

![vehicle22](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37061413/40549019-4f8d42fc-6071-11e8-97a0-d2ed50286d8b.png)
![vehicle77](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37061413/40549021-503e77fc-6071-11e8-941e-0e90b6cc4a06.png)

this is my two drones.
these two drones have same uid. It is my  wondering. The situation that two drones have same value is  normal?

below two pictures are my drones version

![vehicle77-ver](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37061413/40549106-9208b652-6071-11e8-9958-756574145a45.png)
![vehicle22-ver](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37061413/40549110-934ee00e-6071-11e8-9636-02733ded7cb2.png)
Any my drones have PixRacer. AUTOPILOT_VERSION's uid and uid2 are same. But, ver'UIDs are different.

That's odd, the uid and uid2 should be taken from the STM32 UUID of the chip, so that shouldn't happen.

I suggest you create an issue in PX4/Firmware and add all the detail for the two Pixracers.

Thanks. I create an issue in PX4/Firmware.
What isUUID's role in dronecore? It is important?
If is not, I try to replace UUID to system ID.
yer, system ID should work too. Thea idea was to use UUID to be able to refer to individual vehicles over time and not just per session but that's currently not used yet anyway.

> @julianoes Is the MAVLink ID provided some how by the SDK?

No, only the UUID for now. Let's close this because the PX4 Firmware issue has been fixed and follow up in #486.
@mzahana oops.. I missed your message. In my case, I edit dronecode SDK to use sys ID not a UUID. As you see this post, UUID has some problem to me. If you want, I will show this code.
Could you describe the problem that you are facing?
I am working with a set of ordered drones. They have unique NAVLink IDs. So, it is easier for me to deal with system IDs than UUIDs.

@Seunghwan17 I saw that system_id is available [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/core/system_impl.cpp#L518)

The discussion is moved to https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/issues/486

issue.title: Multiple UUIDs for Dronecode SDK
issue.body:
**Feature Request**
I wanted to simulate the offboard control of multiple PX4's using DroneCode. Unfortunately, it so happens that DroneCore distinguishes between PX4's using UUIDs, and all PX4 instances start with the same UUID. It does have another feature where if there is no UUID is available, it will fallback to using the system IDs. So it would be useful if we had the option to declare the UUIDs for each drone, let PX4 set different UUIDs for each vehicle or disable them completely.

Here is the link of the issue I raised in DroneCore : https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/353
